_notes.bolt: A bolt’s damage is `damage` out to falloff[0] metres, falling to damageFar at falloff[1] and damageFar beyond. What it hits takes the cell’s multiplier × that when the product reaches the cell’s threshold, else nothing; a pair with no relation takes noRelation’s cell, 0× under 2 (findings/62 §3).
_notes.fighter: A fighter’s health loses multiplier(bolt.property, fighter.property) × damage × vehicleDamageModifier when multiplier × damage reaches the threshold. fighter.property is the property of its VehicleEntityData.MaterialPair, whichever part the bolt met, because a part’s own relation spends only that part’s states, which reach the health only through a weak spot, and no starfighter has one (findings/62 §2). A friend’s bolt is × friendlyDamageModifier while friendly fire is off. A turret is a vehicle and takes a bolt the same way, against its own property.
_notes.capital: A capital’s part (a static model’s) loses multiplier(bolt.property, part.property) × damage when that reaches the threshold, then × (1 + n × squadBonus.perMate) where `squad` (n the shooter’s squadmates who hit it within squadBonus.cooldown seconds, at most 1 unless eachMate) and × damageMultiplier; a friend’s bolt does nothing unless friendlyFire (findings/62 §4).
_notes.chain: A part starts at health[0] and is spent down its states: a hit never takes it past the next state’s health, where it is held and moves to that state, and the rest of the hit goes back through the same rule (the threshold checked again, so a rest under it is dropped; the squad bonus and damageMultiplier applied again); in the last state it falls to 0. Only a hit on the part its state names (`states`, null for the whole object) spends it, and a state whose part is no longer the part hit sends its `children` FLT_MAX (findings/62 §4). A chain whose first state is one more than its second on a part no bolt hurts (an MC80 nodule’s 201 then 200, a Venator bridge’s 700 then 699) cannot be started by a bolt; what moves it on was not read.
_notes.blast: A blast (a bolt’s `blast`, its ExplosionEntityData) reaches a vehicle through its health component’s slot 43 (FUN_141bea1c0), which applies the record’s damage without a grid multiplier; that was read only so far (findings/62 §3), and whether a blast is held to the grid on a static model was not: `blast` is the record’s, its property beside it, for the damage rules to apply as they rule.
_notes.site: The `site` and `turretParts` blocks are the site’s choices (source: site), not records: which game record each of the war’s part names takes (its numbers then the record’s, with their sources) and which hull parts a turret record stands for, each with why. A hull part no site entry names counts as the hull. An entry with `states` (its record a kit module) spends its chain only on a hit on the hull part its current state names, as the game does (findings/62 §4); one without takes any hit on its `parts`: a site hull’s own part (the Lucrehulk’s, the Arquitens’, a stand-in’s subsystems), or a level’s object outside the kit (the Venator’s bridge and engines, the MC80’s engines), whose states name that object’s own parts, not the hull’s.
_notes.precedence: A hit on a part a `site` entry names spends that entry’s chain (the war’s part), not the part’s own chain in `parts`, which stays as the record has it; a hit on a part `turretParts` names is a hit on that turret.
_notes.assumed: Assumed, as findings/62 leaves it open: a hit’s part is the Havok instance tag’s bits 0–15 (the exporter’s reading of hknpShape::m_userData, PhysicsExport.cs:367, which the data fits); the game’s code that keeps it was not followed.
_notes.dropped: 71 capital parts are left out: every state on a property no bolt here hurts (p132, p0, p34), and neither the site nor a turret names them; a hit on one does nothing.
